answer.generated: Vertical partitioning divides an entity into multiple subentities based on attribute groups, each with fewer attributes than the original. This reduces the number of attributes per subentity, allowing efficient retrieval of large amounts of data with a single access. In contrast, horizontal partitioning splits an entity across tables, which may require more joins and thus less efficient access. Therefore, vertical partitioning is particularly useful when a query accesses many attributes from the same entity, as it minimizes the number of attributes scanned.
